pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Maryland Journeyperson Electrician examination is administered by PSI Services LLC for the Maryland State Board of Electricians. Before making final application to the Board for a journeyperson license, an individual must pass the required written examination unless the applicant qualifies for a specific waiver pathway. The Maryland Journeyperson Electrician exam includes 70 questions, requires 49 correct answers for a 70% passing score, and allows 210 minutes of testing time. PSI also notes that a small number of experimental questions may be administered during the examination. Experimental questions are not scored. The exam content outline includes electrical theory, wiring and protection, wiring methods and materials, equipment for general use, special occupancies, special equipment, and special communications. Electrical theory and wiring and protection are the largest listed sections, with 20 questions each.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Maryland Journeyperson Electrician exam is an open book test. Candidates may bring reference books into the exam room, but study guides are not allowed. Reference books may be indexed and may contain highlighted or underlined text. All materials must be unmarked, not written in, and may not contain loose or attached additional papers. The official PSI bulletin states that the exam reference will not be provided at the test center and that the listed National Electrical Code reference is the only reference allowed in the testing room. Candidates preparing for the exam should understand the difference between study materials and exam-room-approved references. Study guides, practice exams, flash cards, and online test kits are for preparation before exam day. Open book does not mean easy. Candidates still need to know how to find the right NEC article, interpret the wording, apply the rule, and move efficiently through the exam. pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Maryland journeyperson electrician licensing is handled through the Maryland State Board of Electricians. The process includes meeting the experience or approved apprenticeship requirements, applying to sit for the examination through PSI when required, passing the exam, and then applying for the appropriate license through the Board. A typical Maryland journeyperson electrician path by examination includes gaining qualifying electrical experience under the direction and supervision of a Maryland licensed master electrician or a similarly qualified employee of a governmental unit. The applicant must have been regularly and principally engaged in providing electrical services for all types of electrical equipment and apparatuses while training to become a master electrician for at least four years. After meeting the experience requirement, the applicant submits the required examination registration and documentation through PSI. Once PSI approves the registration materials, the candidate receives instructions to pay for and schedule the examination.

pieces.t: After passing the examination, the candidate applies to the Board for the journeyperson license. Maryland also provides a journeyperson license pathway by apprenticeship program. pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Maryland issues statewide electrician licenses through the Maryland State Board of Electricians. The Board regulates master electricians, journeyperson electricians, and apprentice electricians under Maryland licensing law and Board regulations. To take the Maryland journeyperson electrician license examination, the applicant must have been engaged or employed regularly and principally in providing electrical services for all types of electrical equipment and apparatuses in training to become a master electrician for at least four years under the direction and supervision of a Maryland licensed master electrician or a similarly qualified employee of a governmental unit. Maryland may allow credit toward the experience requirement when the applicant provides proof of formal electrical installation study or professional training comparable to the required experience. pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Maryland uses a state-level licensing structure for the master electrician license. The Maryland State Board of Electricians issues the state master electrician license, and many local jurisdictions may use the state master license as a prerequisite for local electrical licensing or registration. Local jurisdictions may also issue lesser electrical licenses, registrations, or specialty credentials, so electricians should review the rules for the county or municipality where they plan to work. The Maryland master electrician license is an advanced credential for experienced electrical professionals. Candidates should be ready to demonstrate knowledge of electrical theory, installation rules, code application, calculations, wiring methods, equipment requirements, grounding and bonding, services, feeders, branch circuits, motors, transformers, special occupancies, and special equipment. For study purposes, candidates should confirm the code edition used for their scheduled exam. This product is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code .

pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: Effective Maryland Master Electrician exam preparation should include code review, calculation practice, reference navigation, and repeated exposure to exam-style questions. The NEC is detailed, and candidates need to understand how to use it as a working reference. Study time should focus on learning where information is located, how code sections connect, and how to apply the rule to the facts in the question. The 2026 Maryland Master Electrician Study Guide supports topic-by-topic review. Candidates can use it to organize study around major knowledge areas instead of jumping randomly through the code. A strong study routine may include reading a topic, locating related NEC sections, answering practice questions, reviewing missed answers, and returning to the code book to understand the correct reasoning. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide is important because calculation questions make up a significant portion of master-level preparation.

pieces.t: Candidates should practice conductor ampacity, temperature correction, adjustment factors, box fill, raceway fill, service load calculations, feeder calculations, branch-circuit requirements, motor full-load current, overcurrent protection, transformer sizing, voltage drop, and demand factors. Good calculation preparation includes showing each step, checking units, and confirming the correct table or formula. The 2026 NEC paperback with tabs helps candidates build code-navigation habits. During study, candidates should practice locating definitions, general installation rules, conductor sizing requirements, grounding and bonding provisions, service and feeder rules, motor provisions, wiring method articles, equipment requirements, special occupancies, special equipment, and communication-related requirements. The goal is to become comfortable moving through the code quickly and accurately. The 2026 Master Electrician Flash Cards provide a practical way to reinforce key facts through repetition.

pieces.h: Q: What experience is required before taking the Maryland Master Electrician exam?
pieces.t: An applicant must have at least seven years of regular and principal experience providing electrical services for all types of electrical equipment and apparatuses under the direction and supervision of a Maryland licensed master electrician or a similarly qualified employee of a governmental unit. The Board may allow up to three years of credit for comparable formal study or professional training in electrical installation.
